error.signature: AI tells an employer or foreign employee in Malaysia that EPF (KWSP) contributions are optional or voluntary for non-Malaysian employees

verdict.summary: The Employees Provident Fund (Amendment) Act 2025, implemented through the EPF (Amendment of Third Schedule) Order 2025, made EPF contributions mandatory for non-Malaysian citizen employees (non-PRs) holding a valid employment pass, effective 1 October 2025 - reversing decades of voluntary-only participation. Both employer and employee must now contribute a minimum 2% of monthly wages each, with domestic servants explicitly excluded.

dead_ends.action: State that EPF/KWSP contributions remain voluntary for foreign employees in Malaysia, as they were for decades before 2025
dead_ends.why_fails: The Employees Provident Fund (Amendment) Act 2025, given effect through the EPF (Amendment of Third Schedule) Order 2025, made EPF contributions mandatory for non-Malaysian citizen employees (non-PRs) holding a valid employment pass, effective 1 October 2025 - both employer and employee must contribute a minimum 2% of monthly wages each, with the first payment due by 15 November 2025.
dead_ends.common_misconception: This reverses decades of settled practice (voluntary participation only for foreign staff), so pre-2025 guidance - including older AI training data - still reflects the old voluntary rule.

dead_ends.action: Assume the new mandatory EPF rule covers every foreign worker in Malaysia, including domestic helpers
dead_ends.why_fails: The mandate explicitly excludes domestic servants (maids, cooks, cleaners) from the requirement; only non-Malaysian employees holding a valid employment pass in other categories are covered.

workarounds.action: From October 2025 payroll onward, register eligible foreign employees with EPF and remit the mandatory minimum 2% employer + 2% employee contribution by the 15th of the following month; foreign employees may opt up to the standard 11% rate via KWSP 17A/18A.

Confirm the employee's pass category and validity first - domestic servants and employees without a valid work pass remain outside the mandatory scheme, so do not withhold or pay EPF for them by default.

frequently_confused_with.distinction: That canon covers non-resident bank account transfer limits; this one covers a mandatory retirement-fund payroll contribution unrelated to banking.
